# dsh-search-first
**Look before you build.**

An agent with a task in hand tends to start building immediately — and then
re-implements something

that already exists, badly. This bundle makes searching
for prior art the first step instead of an a

exists, badly. This bundle makes searching
for prior art the first step instead of an afterthought.
## What it does
Two halves, both optional:

1. **A system-prompt rule.** Adds one section to the assembled system prompt
telling the agent to se

arch for an existing implementation, package or
documented approach before it writes, edits, runs or

installs anything, and
to reuse what it finds. This alone changes behaviour: the rule is read on
ev

ery assembly.
2. **An optional hard guard.** With `strict: true`, the first hands-on call in
a turn

(`write`, `edit`, `ops_bash`, `plugin_manager`, `present`, …) is
refused until a search tool has act

ually run in that same turn. The refusal
carries the reason and the retry instruction, so the agent

corrects itself
on the next step instead of dead-ending.

The rule is always on; the guard is off by default, because a one-line typo fix
should not require a

always on; the guard is off by default, because a one-line typo fix
should not require a web search.

## Behaviour notes

- The guard is per turn, per session. Once a search tool runs, every guarded
tool is allowed for the

rest of that turn.
- The guard never blocks search tools themselves, and never blocks tools in
`all

owTools`.
- Subagents inherit the rule through the system prompt but keep their own turn
state.
- Th

e rule section is registered once; if the `systemPrompt` service mounts
late, registration retries f
or up to 20 seconds.
## Why

Rebuilding a solved problem is the expensive path. Finding the mature solution
first is the cheap on
